items.title: Please comment on CVE-2024-53899 and virtualenv activation scripts
items.reason: Historical activation-script command-injection discussion. Maintainers identified environment-path quoting fixes and treated quoting defects as bugs. Those fixes did not escape prompt values, so this is related context rather than a duplicate.

items.title: Allow apostrophe in venv name
items.reason: Merged on 2024-11-15 to fix astral-sh/uv#8947. Its diff escapes VIRTUAL_ENV_DIR for single-quoted assignments but leaves VIRTUAL_PROMPT interpolation unchanged. The current prompt bug falls outside that fix.

items.title: Venv configuration readback can reinterpret path boundaries
items.reason: Another uv 0.13.6 report involving --prompt and directory names. It concerns newlines injecting pyvenv.cfg directives and changing isolation; this report concerns shell evaluation. The output formats and required fixes differ.

items.title: 🐛 fix(bash): preserve literal prompts in supported shells
items.reason: Upstream PR corresponding to the reporter's linked commit, merged on 2026-10-17. It addresses PS1 rendering under Bash compatibility levels, promptvars, and POSIX mode. It informs a rendering fix but does not fix uv's separate source-time interpolation.

related.search_scope: Used authenticated gh searches across astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs. Separately searched source-time substitution, directory-derived prompts, and compatibility modes using CVE-2026-113723, command substitution, PS1, VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT, BASH_COMPAT, promptvars, Bash/POSIX, backticks, dollars, and backslashes. Conceptual searches covered activation injection, command execution, prompt escaping, literal prompts, directory quoting, and special characters, including area:environments. Fix-oriented searches covered activation, prompt, and escaping PRs; inspected 1,000 recent PR titles and followed astral-sh/uv#9424 through astral-sh/uv#8947, astral-sh/uv#8984, and astral-sh/uv#9466, plus the upstream commit and pypa/virtualenv#3418. Inspected comments and ruled out astral-sh/uv#13456 (prompt formatting), astral-sh/uv#12662 (SCRIPT_PATH leakage), astral-sh/uv#10498 (unset OSTYPE), and astral-sh/uv#5950 (printed Windows activation paths). No same-problem uv tracker or prompt fix was found.

type_reason: The current generator inserts explicit prompt text unescaped into double-quoted activation code. A harmless check of the checkout's template in Bash 5.2 confirmed command substitution during activation; a separate check confirmed directory-derived text is evaluated when rendering PS1. These are correctness defects regardless of security classification. The historical path-quoting fix did not cover prompt interpolation, so this is not an established regression of that fix. No existing uv issue or PR was found that tracks the same problem.
summary: No uv duplicate found. astral-sh/uv#9424 and astral-sh/uv#8984 document earlier path quoting; astral-sh/uv#23054 concerns a different prompt serialization defect. Upstream pypa/virtualenv#3418 addresses compatibility-sensitive prompt rendering.
draft_response:
Your `--prompt` example exposes a bug in the current activation template: the value is inserted unescaped into double-quoted shell code, allowing command substitution while sourcing it, including in ordinary Bash. The path-quoting fix in astral-sh/uv#8984, discussed in astral-sh/uv#9424, does not cover this value.

Directory-derived prompts differ: `basename` preserves the text during activation, but Bash can evaluate it when rendering `PS1`. The next step is to fix both script-generation quoting and prompt rendering, with regression coverage for explicit prompts, directory names, and Bash compatibility/POSIX settings. Upstream pypa/virtualenv#3418 is relevant to rendering, but does not by itself address uv's source-time interpolation.
